narrative.northStar: Product-grade, in the visitor's own light
narrative.overview:
The page sells infrastructure the way the best developer platforms do: by showing the product working, held to Stripe- and Linear-grade polish. It follows the visitor's system setting: a near-black canvas with crisp white hairlines, or white paper with graphite hairlines, quiet layered surfaces, a white primary button that means "act here" and a blue that means "this is the agent, or a link". Every illustration is real-looking product UI (a partner's app with our agent inside, a run receipt, a webhook payload, a credit ledger, a code editor), never concept art or diagrams of our internals. The claim "the controls are real" is made by drawing the controls.

Density is product-like rather than editorial. Sections pair a short balanced headline and a lede with a panel of evidence: ids in mono, tabular figures, status tags and meters. Ornament is limited to one faint, cool light behind the hero product. Restraint is the enterprise signal: each section makes one point with one piece of evidence, and nothing is said twice. Motion is spent once per page, on the hero chat loop, so it reads as a demonstration rather than decoration.

The system descends from the incumbent near-black-and-blue brand but deliberately retires its glowing effects: no gradient text, no glass, no particles. It also stands apart from the earlier looks that PRODUCT.md records as rejected.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes from one token set, chosen by prefers-color-scheme; code panels and the terminal stay ink in both
One atmosphere opens and closes each page: an arc of blue light over a field of customer workspaces, the awake ones glowing
Near-black canvas (#07080b) with layered surfaces separated by white-alpha hairlines, never heavy borders
One blue family for every interactive and accent role; green, amber and red appear only as state
Real product UI as illustration, every piece of demo data labelled illustrative
Geist for everything, at a single 600 heading weight with tight negative tracking; Geist Mono for ids, code and figures
Soft, rounded product geometry (6 to 16px), depth from dark drop shadows and a 1px top highlight
One authored motion moment per page: the hero's partner-app chat
RTL-ready through logical properties, with ids and code pinned LTR

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue is the only interactive and accent colour. If it is clickable, focused, selected or highlighted, it is blue. Nothing else takes an accent hue, apart from the syntax palette inside code.

rules.name: The Partner Colour Rule
rules.body: Partner Brand appears only inside the illustrated partner app ("your app": the hero window, and its mark in the statement rail and the harness map). It is never used for an OpenLegion button, link, heading or surface. The test: covering the partner app should leave no orange on the page.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean ok, held and danger. They are never decoration, never a section colour and never a heading colour.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Every heading, from Display down to Title, is Geist 600 with negative tracking that tightens as size grows (-0.012em up to -0.04em). Hierarchy comes from size and colour, never from a second display face or a heavier weight.

rules.name: The Pinned Figures Rule
rules.body: Ids, tool names, credits, timestamps and code are set dir="ltr", and counts use tabular numerals, so they read identically on Arabic pages.

rules.name: The Shadow-Is-Black Rule
rules.body: Shadows are black, never coloured. The only coloured light is the single blue hero glow, and it sits behind product UI, never under text as an effect on the text itself.

rules.name: The One-Token-Set Rule
rules.body: A component reads tokens and never checks the theme. A colour that only works in one theme becomes a token with a value for each theme, never a second rule. Ink islands (code panels, the terminal, article pre) redeclare the dark palette on themselves.

dos: Do use the blue family for every interactive and accent role: Action Blue fills, Signal Blue links and focus, Blue Ink for blue text on dark.
Do keep Partner Brand (#ff6b3d) inside the illustrated partner app only.
Do use ok, hold and danger for state alone (tags, discs, approval, meters).
Do illustrate with real product UI (app windows, receipts, ledgers, payloads, code) and label every piece of demo data illustrative in a Fine caption.
Do lay mechanisms out as an uneven bento with a working mini visual in each cell.
Do keep one authored motion moment per page, the hero chat. Pause it out of view, and give reduced motion and no-JS a still frame.
Do draw icons on the 16-unit grid with a 1.6 round stroke in currentColor.
Do use logical properties (ms/me/ps/pe, text-start/text-end) and pin ids, code and figures dir="ltr".
Do keep 20px gutters on mobile with no horizontal scroll, and hide the hero app sidebar and tabs at 640px and below.
Do style learn and comparison articles only through the shared prose layer, because their copy is SEO-locked.
Do check every new colour in both themes; keep theme-specific values in tokens and keep code and the terminal ink.
donts: Don't put an eyebrow or kicker label above a heading.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism, particles or coloured glows on text.
Don't use unicode glyphs (arrows, checks, stars) as icons.
Don't add a coloured border-left (or border-start) accent to any block.
Don't build an equal grid of icon cards for features.
Don't use Partner Brand, or any state colour, as an OpenLegion accent.
Don't add a second animated sequence, scroll-triggered reveals or looping decoration outside the hero.
Don't present demo ids, figures or logos as real usage.
Don't hard-code white or black washes outside the ink islands; use --tint-* or color-mix() with a token.
Don't use the syntax palette (.tok-*) outside a code panel; on the page, code-like labels take Blue Ink.
Don't put the atmosphere field behind text; mark copy data-field-copy and captions data-field-clear.
